# RAG Index Directory

This directory stores the generated vector index files for the Nova RAG system.

## Contents (generated by extract_data.py → build_index.py)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `documents.json` | Document chunks with metadata (id, content, source, title) |
| `embeddings.json` | Vector embeddings (1024 dimensions, normalized) |
| `metadata.json` | Index metadata (version, stats, build time, data_hash) |

## Index Statistics (last build: 2026-09-04)

- **Total chunks**: 563
- **Total source documents**: 92
- **Embedding dimension**: 1024 (bge-large-zh-v1.5)
- **Source distribution**: project(8), personal(1), blog(17), project_doc(66)
- **data_hash**: see `metadata.json`

## Build

`build_index.py` only reads `rag/data/extracted_content.json`; it does **not** re-extract.
After changing `data/*.ts`, `content/blog/*.mdx`, or `docs/projects/*.md`, run **both** in order:

```bash
python rag/scripts/extract_data.py     # re-extract source → rag/data/extracted_content.json
npm run rag:build                       # chunk + embed → public/rag-index/*.json
```

> Reversing the order (or running only `rag:build`) makes the source-hash check falsely
> report "up to date" and silently drops new content. For GPU speed use the CUDA venv
> (`D:/python/project/.venv`) rather than `rag/venv` (CPU torch).

## Note

These files are **committed to git** (so `npm run build`/deploy needs no Python), despite
`embeddings.json` being ~12 MB. There is no runtime embedding service — search uses a
pseudo-query vector (average of top keyword-matched doc embeddings).
